title: heat-pulse workload runner and per-kernel flamepoint reporter for spike-resilience profiling
author: Elena Park
description: ### Motivation: Production inference workloads occasionally experience short, high-intensity token bursts that expose kernel-level hotspots and transient queuing behavior not visible in steady-state runners. This PR introduces a new heat-pulse workload runner that synthesizes variable-length burst patterns with configurable quiescent intervals, and a companion per-kernel flamepoint reporter that attributes execution time and memory pressure to specific kernels across burst phases. ### What: Adds heat_pulse_runner (Rust) which supports: parameterized pulse shapes (gaussian, uniform, heavy-tail), sequence-length jittering, client-side KV-cache hit/miss toggles, and an extensible output format for sample-level traces. Adds flamepoint_reporter (Python) that ingests sample traces and per-kernel telemetry (GPU/HW counters, CUDA kernel names, cpu-wire timestamps) and emits kernel-level flamecharts, burst-aligned aggregated summaries, and a small CSV pivot for correlation with scheduler events. Also wires up CI bench job, docs, and sample configurations. ### Why: Existing runners focus on steady throughput or synthetic mixes that underrepresent short spikes; this change lets us reproduce production microbursts and attribute regressions to kernels or scheduling artifacts, enabling targeted mitigations (batching windows, kernel fusion, preemption tuning). ### Implementation notes: heat_pulse_runner implements an event scheduler that replays request arrival times from a generated pulse series and supports CSV export of per-request metadata. The runner is implemented in bench/runners/heat_pulse_runner.rs and shares common client helpers in bench/utils. The flamepoint reporter lives in bench/reporters/flamepoint_reporter.py and depends on an optional rust->json trace exporter. CI: bench-ci includes an optional job that runs a short heat-pulse profile on a single GPU instance; artifacts include flamepoint HTML and CSV. ### Tests and validation: Unit tests cover pulse generator distributions and sample export; integration test runs a short burst profile in CI with mocked telemetry to assert exporter schema. Local runs on our perf cluster show that heavy-tail pulses expose a previously unnoticed 9-12% P95 regression when the cuda_mmapped kernel queues overlap with kv-cache refills. ### Backwards compatibility: All existing runners unchanged; flamepoint_reporter is optional and only used when per-kernel telemetry is available. ### How to use: see docs/bench/heat-pulse.md for config examples and a step-by-step recipe to reproduce the microburst scenario. ### Related: ENG-2476 for tracking followups around automated mitigation heuristics and ENG-2531 for a downstream remediation experiment.

review_comments: Ravi Patel: Nice overall shape. A couple of asks: 1) make pulse seedable for reproducibility in CI, 2) ensure the exporter includes kernel name hashes so we can join with kernel catalog later.
Author (Elena): addressed both; added --seed flag and kernel_name_hash field to CSV export (see commit c3e5f10).
Noah Kim: can you reduce the default sample export verbosity? Large traces blow up S3 costs in nightly runs.
Author (Elena): reduced default sampling to 1/10 and added --full-trace toggle; documented retention guidance in docs.
Sophie Laurent: approved after CI green and documentation added.
release_notes: Add heat-pulse workload runner and flamepoint reporter to reproduce and analyze short-duration microburst workloads. Useful for kernel-level hotspot attribution and scheduler tuning.
